Given below are two statements:
$R=8.314$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$ and $1$ cal $=4.2$ J
Statement I: When $E_a=12.6$ kcal/mol, the room temperature rate constant is doubled by a $10\,^\circ$C increase in temperature ($298$ K to $308$ K)
Statement II: For a first order reactions A $\rightarrow$ B,

Here $[A]_o$ is the initial concentration of A and $t_{1/2}$ is half life of reaction.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.solution:
For Statement I:
According to the Arrhenius equation:
$\log \left( \dfrac{k_2}{k_1} \right) = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R} \left( \dfrac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2} \right)$

Given that the rate constant doubles, $k_2 = 2k_1$. The temperatures are $T_1 = 298$ K and $T_2 = 308$ K.
The gas constant $R = 8.314$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1} = \dfrac{8.314}{4.2}$ cal K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1} \approx 1.98$ cal K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$.

Substituting the values:
$\log(2) = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 \times 1.98} \left( \dfrac{308 - 298}{298 \times 308} \right)$

$0.301 = \dfrac{E_a}{4.56} \left( \dfrac{10}{91784} \right)$

$E_a = \dfrac{0.301 \times 4.56 \times 91784}{10} \approx 12598$ cal/mol $\approx 12.6$ kcal/mol.
Thus, Statement I is true.

For Statement II:
For a first order reaction, the half-life is given by:
$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{k}$
This indicates that the half-life of a first order reaction is independent of the initial concentration $[A]_o$. The graph of $t_{1/2}$ versus $[A]_o$ should be a horizontal line parallel to the concentration axis.
The given graph shows $t_{1/2}$ directly proportional to $[A]_o$, which corresponds to a zero order reaction ($t_{1/2} = \dfrac{[A]_o}{2k}$).
Thus, Statement II is false.

Therefore, Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

Answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Decomposition of a hydrocarbon follows the equation $k = (5.5 \times 10^{11}\,\text{s}^{-1})\,e^{\frac{-28000\,\text{K}}{T}}$. The activation energy of reaction is __________ kJ mol$^{-1}$. (Nearest Integer) Given : R $= 8.3$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$
questions.solution:
According to the Arrhenius equation, $k = A e^{-\dfrac{E_a}{RT}}$.

The given equation is $k = (5.5 \times 10^{11} \text{ s}^{-1}) e^{-\dfrac{28000}{T}}$.

Comparing the exponent of $e$ in both equations:

$\dfrac{E_a}{RT} = \dfrac{28000}{T}$

$E_a = 28000 \times R$

Substituting the value of $R = 8.3 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$:

$E_a = 28000 \times 8.3 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$

$E_a = 232400 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$

$E_a = 232.4 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, the activation energy is $232$.

Answer: $232$

questions.q:
For a reaction $A \rightarrow P$ at $T\text{ K}$, the half life $(t_{1/2})$ is plotted as a function of initial concentration $[A]_0$ of $A$ as given below.

The value of $x$ in the given figure is _______ s (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
From the given graph, the plot of half-life $t_{1/2}$ versus initial concentration $[A]_0$ is a straight line passing through the origin.

This indicates that $t_{1/2}$ is directly proportional to $[A]_0$, which means $t_{1/2} \propto [A]_0$.

Therefore, the ratio $\dfrac{t_{1/2}}{[A]_0}$ is constant.

Using the coordinates from the graph, we get:

$\dfrac{240}{4 \times 10^{-3}} = \dfrac{x}{1.5 \times 10^{-3}}$

Solving for $x$:

$x = \dfrac{240 \times 1.5 \times 10^{-3}}{4 \times 10^{-3}}$

$x = 60 \times 1.5 = 90$

The value of $x$ is $90$.

Answer: $90$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
First order gas phase reaction $A \rightarrow B + C$
$p_i =$ initial pressure of gas A, $p_t =$ total pressure of the reaction mixture at time $t$
Expression of rate constant ($k$) is
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $A(g) \rightarrow B(g) + C(g)$

At $t = 0$, the initial pressure of A is $p_i$ and the pressures of B and C are $0$.

At time $t$, let the decrease in pressure of A be $x$.
Pressure of A $= p_i - x$
Pressure of B $= x$
Pressure of C $= x$

Total pressure at time $t$ is $p_t = (p_i - x) + x + x = p_i + x$

From this, we get $x = p_t - p_i$

The partial pressure of A at time $t$ is $P_A = p_i - x = p_i - (p_t - p_i) = 2p_i - p_t$

For a first order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by

$k = \dfrac{1}{t}\ln\dfrac{P_{A,0}}{P_A}$

Substituting the values, we get

$k = \dfrac{1}{t}\ln\dfrac{p_i}{2p_i - p_t}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{t}\ln\dfrac{p_i}{2p_i - p_t}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
If the half life of a first order reaction is $6.93$ minutes then the time required for completion of $99$% of the reaction will be _____ minutes.
(Given : $\log 2 = 0.3010$)
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by:

$k = \dfrac{2.303 \log 2}{t_{1/2}}$

Using the standard approximation $2.303 \log 2 \approx 0.693$:

$k = \dfrac{0.693}{6.93} = 0.1 \text{ min}^{-1}$

The time required for $99\%$ completion of the reaction is given by the integrated rate law:

$t = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \dfrac{a}{a - x} \right)$

Here, the initial concentration $a = 100$ and the amount reacted $x = 99$, so $a - x = 1$.

$t = \dfrac{2.303}{0.1} \log \left( \dfrac{100}{1} \right)$

$t = 23.03 \times \log(10^2)$

$t = 23.03 \times 2 = 46.06 \text{ minutes}$

Answer: $46.06$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the given graph showing variation of reactant concentration with time.
Three different reactions were started with identical initial concentration of reactants. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: The order of all the three reactions is same.
The rate constant of reaction $3$ is larger than the rate constant of reaction $2$ if the order of reaction is same for both.
The SI unit of rate constant of reaction $1$ is s$^{-1}$.
Thermal decomposition of HI on gold surface is an example of reaction $2$.
questions.solution:
Analysis of the graph:
The graph shows reactant concentration $[R]$ vs time $t$ for three reactions starting from the same initial concentration.

Curve 1 is a straight line with negative slope. For a zero-order reaction, the integrated rate law is $[R] = [R]_0 - kt$, which is a straight line in $[R]$ vs $t$. Hence, reaction $1$ is a zero-order reaction.

Curves 2 and 3 are non-linear (exponential-type decays), so they correspond to reactions of order greater than zero (e.g., first or second order).

Evaluating the options:

$(1)$ The order of all three reactions is the same.
Reaction $1$ is zero order while reactions $2$ and $3$ are of higher order, so this statement is incorrect.

$(2)$ The rate constant of reaction $3$ is larger than that of reaction $2$, assuming both have the same order.
Assuming both curves $2$ and $3$ correspond to the same order (say first order), the integrated rate law is $[R] = [R]_0 e^{-kt}$. At any given time $t$, the curve for reaction $3$ lies below that of reaction $2$, i.e., $[R]_3 < [R]_2$. Since both start from the same $[R]_0$, reaction $3$ is decaying faster, which implies a larger rate constant. Hence $k_3 > k_2$, and this statement is correct.

$(3)$ The SI unit of the rate constant of reaction $1$ is $\text{s}^{-1}$.
For a zero-order reaction, $\text{Rate} = k[R]^0 = k$, so the unit of $k$ is that of rate, i.e., $\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$. The unit $\text{s}^{-1}$ corresponds to a first-order reaction, so this statement is incorrect.

$(4)$ Thermal decomposition of $HI$ on a gold surface is an example of reaction $2$.
The thermal decomposition of $HI$ on a gold surface is a well-known zero-order reaction, which corresponds to curve $1$, not curve $2$. Hence this statement is incorrect.

Therefore, the correct option is $(2)$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For a first order reaction $A \rightarrow B$
$t/\text{min}$$[A]/M$
$0$$0.6500$
$x$$0.0650$
$20$$0.00065$

$x=$ ______ min. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by:

$k = \dfrac{1}{t} \ln \dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]_t}$

Using the data at $t = 20$ min:

$k = \dfrac{1}{20} \ln \dfrac{0.6500}{0.00065} = \dfrac{1}{20} \ln 1000 = \dfrac{3}{20} \ln 10$

Using the data at $t = x$ min:

$k = \dfrac{1}{x} \ln \dfrac{0.6500}{0.0650} = \dfrac{1}{x} \ln 10$

Equating the two expressions for $k$:

$\dfrac{3}{20} \ln 10 = \dfrac{1}{x} \ln 10$

$\dfrac{3}{20} = \dfrac{1}{x}$

$x = \dfrac{20}{3} = 6.66...$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we get $x = 7$.

Answer: $7$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider the first order reaction $R \rightarrow P$. The fraction of molecules decomposed in the given first order reaction can be expressed as
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, the concentration of reactant at time $t$ is given by

$[R]_t = [R]_0 e^{-k_1 t}$

The amount of reactant decomposed is

$[R]_0 - [R]_t = [R]_0 - [R]_0 e^{-k_1 t} = [R]_0 (1 - e^{-k_1 t})$

The fraction of molecules decomposed is

$\dfrac{[R]_0 - [R]_t}{[R]_0} = \dfrac{[R]_0 (1 - e^{-k_1 t})}{[R]_0} = 1 - e^{-k_1 t}$

Answer: $1 - e^{-k_1 t}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the reaction $aX \rightarrow bY$, for which the rate constant at $30°C$ is $1 \times 10^{-3}$ mol$^{-1}$ L s$^{-1}$. Which of the following statements are true?
A. When concentration of 'X' is increased to four times, the rate of reaction becomes $16$ times.
B. The reaction is a second order reaction.
C. The half-life period is independent of the concentration of X.
D. Decomposition of $N_2 O_5$ is an example of the above reaction.
E. $\ln\dfrac{[R_o]}{[R]}$ vs time is valid for the above reaction.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, D and E Only
questions.solution:
The unit of the rate constant $k$ is mol$^{-1}$ L s$^{-1}$.

The general unit of the rate constant for an $n$-th order reaction is (mol L$^{-1}$)$^{1-n}$ s$^{-1}$.

Equating the powers of the concentration units, we get $1-n = -1 \Rightarrow n = 2$.

Thus, the reaction is a second-order reaction. Statement B is correct.

For a second-order reaction, Rate $= k[X]^2$. When the concentration of $X$ is increased to $4$ times, the new rate is $k(4[X])^2 = 16k[X]^2$, which is $16$ times the original rate. Statement A is correct.

The half-life of a second-order reaction is $t_{1/2} = \dfrac{1}{k[X]_0}$, which depends inversely on the initial concentration. Statement C is incorrect.

The decomposition of $N_2O_5$ is a well-known first-order reaction. Statement D is incorrect.

The equation $\ln\dfrac{[R_o]}{[R]} = kt$ represents the integrated rate law for a first-order reaction, not a second-order reaction. Statement E is incorrect.

Therefore, only statements A and B are correct.

Answer: A and B Only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following gas phase reaction being carried out in a closed vessel at $25°C$.
$2A(g) \rightarrow 4B(g) + C(g)$
time (min)total pressure of the system (mm Hg)
$30$$300$
$\infty$$600$
The pressure of $C(g)$ at $30$ minutes time interval would be _______ mm Hg. (nearest integer)
questions.solution:
For the given gas phase reaction:

$2A(g) \rightarrow 4B(g) + C(g)$

Let the initial pressure of $A(g)$ be $P_0$.

At $t = 0$: $P_A = P_0$, $P_B = 0$, $P_C = 0$

At $t = t$: $P_A = P_0 - 2p$, $P_B = 4p$, $P_C = p$

Total pressure at time $t$, $P_t = P_0 - 2p + 4p + p = P_0 + 3p$

At $t = \infty$, the reaction is complete, so $P_A = 0 \Rightarrow 2p = P_0 \Rightarrow p = \dfrac{P_0}{2}$

Total pressure at $t = \infty$, $P_{\infty} = 4\left(\dfrac{P_0}{2}\right) + \dfrac{P_0}{2} = \dfrac{5P_0}{2}$

Given $P_{\infty} = 600$ mm Hg:

$\dfrac{5P_0}{2} = 600 \Rightarrow P_0 = 240$ mm Hg

At $t = 30$ min, $P_t = 300$ mm Hg:

$P_0 + 3p = 300$

$240 + 3p = 300 \Rightarrow 3p = 60 \Rightarrow p = 20$ mm Hg

The pressure of $C(g)$ at $30$ minutes is $p = 20$ mm Hg.

Answer: $20$

At $t = t$: $P_A = P_0 - 2p$, $P_B = 4p$, $P_C = p$

Total pressure at time $t$, $P_t = P_0 - 2p + 4p + p = P_0 + 3p$

At $t = \infty$, the reaction is complete, so $P_A = 0 \Rightarrow 2p = P_0 \Rightarrow p = \dfrac{P_0}{2}$

Total pressure at $t = \infty$, $P_{\infty} = 4\left(\dfrac{P_0}{2}\right) + \dfrac{P_0}{2} = \dfrac{5P_0}{2}$

Given $P_{\infty} = 600$ mm Hg:

$\dfrac{5P_0}{2} = 600 \Rightarrow P_0 = 240$ mm Hg

At $t = 30$ min, $P_t = 300$ mm Hg:

$P_0 + 3p = 300$

$240 + 3p = 300 \Rightarrow 3p = 60 \Rightarrow p = 20$ mm Hg

The pressure of $C(g)$ at $30$ minutes is $p = 20$ mm Hg.

Answer: $20$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $t_{100\%}$ is the time required for the $100\%$ completion of the reaction while $t_{1/2}$ is the time required for $50\%$ of the reaction to be completed. Which of the following option correctly represents the relation between $t_{100\%}$ and $t_{1/2}$ for zero and first order reactions respectively?
questions.solution:
For a zero-order reaction:
The integrated rate law is given by $t = \dfrac{[A]_0 - [A]_t}{k}$.

For $50\%$ completion ($t_{1/2}$), $[A]_t = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2}$:
$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{[A]_0 - \dfrac{[A]_0}{2}}{k} = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2k}$

For $100\%$ completion ($t_{100\%}$), $[A]_t = 0$:
$t_{100\%} = \dfrac{[A]_0 - 0}{k} = \dfrac{[A]_0}{k}$

Comparing the two, we get:
$t_{100\%} = 2t_{1/2}$

For a first-order reaction:
The integrated rate law is given by $t = \dfrac{1}{k} \ln\left(\dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]_t}\right)$.

For $100\%$ completion ($t_{100\%}$), $[A]_t = 0$:
$t_{100\%} = \dfrac{1}{k} \ln\left(\dfrac{[A]_0}{0}\right) = \infty$

A first-order reaction takes infinite time for $100\%$ completion. Among the given choices, this is symbolically represented as $\infty$ or $(t_{1/2})^\infty$.

Thus, the correct relation is $t_{100\%} = 2t_{1/2}$ for zero-order and $t_{100\%} = \infty$ for first-order.

Answer: $t_{100\%} = 2t_{1/2}$ and $t_{100\%} = (t_{1/2})^\infty$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For reaction $A \rightarrow P$, rate constant $k = 1.5 \times 10^3$ s$^{-1}$ at $27°$C. If activation energy for the above reaction is $60$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, then the temperature (in $°$C) at which rate constant, $k = 4.5 \times 10^3$ s$^{-1}$ is _______. (Nearest integer)
Given : $\log 2 = 0.30$, $\log 3 = 0.48$, $R = 8.3$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$, $\ln 10 = 2.3$
questions.solution:
Using the Arrhenius equation:

$\log \left( \dfrac{k_2}{k_1} \right) = \dfrac{E_a}{2.3 R} \left( \dfrac{1}{T_1} - \dfrac{1}{T_2} \right)$

Given:
$k_1 = 1.5 \times 10^3 \text{ s}^{-1}$
$k_2 = 4.5 \times 10^3 \text{ s}^{-1}$
$T_1 = 27^\circ\text{C} = 300 \text{ K}$
$E_a = 60 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1} = 60000 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$
$R = 8.3 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$

Substituting the values into the equation:

$\log \left( \dfrac{4.5 \times 10^3}{1.5 \times 10^3} \right) = \dfrac{60000}{2.3 \times 8.3} \left( \dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1}{T_2} \right)$

$\log 3 = \dfrac{60000}{19.09} \left( \dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1}{T_2} \right)$

$0.48 = \dfrac{60000}{19.09} \left( \dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1}{T_2} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1}{T_2} = \dfrac{0.48 \times 19.09}{60000}$

$\dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1}{T_2} = \dfrac{9.1632}{60000} = 1.5272 \times 10^{-4}$

$\dfrac{1}{T_2} = \dfrac{1}{300} - 1.5272 \times 10^{-4}$

$\dfrac{1}{T_2} = 3.3333 \times 10^{-3} - 0.1527 \times 10^{-3} = 3.1806 \times 10^{-3} \text{ K}^{-1}$

$T_2 = \dfrac{1}{3.1806 \times 10^{-3}} \approx 314.4 \text{ K}$

Converting to Celsius:
$T_2 = 314.4 - 273 = 41.4^\circ\text{C}$

The nearest integer is $41$.

Answer: $41$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$\mathrm{A} \longrightarrow \mathrm{B}$ (first reaction)
$\mathrm{C} \longrightarrow \mathrm{D}$ (second reaction)
Consider the above two first-order reactions. The rate constant for first reaction at 500 K is double of the same at 300 K. At $500 \mathrm{~K}, 50 \%$ of the reaction becomes complete in 2 hour. The activation energy of the second reaction is half of that of first reaction. If the rate constant at 500 K of the second reaction becomes double of the rate constant of first reaction at the same temperature; then rate constant for the second reaction at 300 K is $\_\_\_\_$\times 10^{-1}$ hour $^{-1}$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution:
For $A \xrightarrow{K_1} B$
$\ln(2) = \dfrac{E_{a_1}}{R} \left[ \dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1}{500} \right]$
$E_{a_1} = \dfrac{\ln 2 \times R \times 1500}{2}$
$E_{a_2} = \dfrac{E_{a_1}}{2} = \dfrac{\ln 2 \times R \times 1500}{4}$
$(K_1)_{\text{at 500 K}} = \dfrac{\ln 2}{2}$
$(K_2)_{\text{at 500 K}} = \ln 2$
Now for $C \xrightarrow{K_2} D$
$\ln \left[ \dfrac{(K_2)_{\text{at 500K}}}{(K_2)_{\text{at 300K}}} \right] = \left( \dfrac{\ln 2 \times R \times 1500}{4} \right) \times \dfrac{1}{R} \times \left[ \dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1}{500} \right]$
$(K_2)_{\text{at 300 K}} = \dfrac{\ln 2}{\sqrt{2}} = 0.49$
$(K_2)_{\text{at 300 K}} = 4.9 \times 10^{-1}$.
So, answer is 5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound undergoes first order decomposition. The time taken for decomposition to $\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{\text{th }}$ and $\left(\frac{1}{10}\right)^{\text{th }}$ of its initial concentration are $\mathrm{t}_{1 / 8}$ and $\mathrm{t}_{1 / 10}$ respectively. What is the value of $\frac{\mathrm{t}_{1 / 8}}{\mathrm{t}_{1 / 10}} \times 10$ ? ($\log 2=0.3$)
questions.solution:
For first-order decomposition with rate equation $[A] = [A]_0 e^{-kt}$, the time for concentration to reduce to fraction f is: $t = \frac{1}{k}\ln\frac{1}{f} = \frac{\ln(1/f)}{k}$
For reduction to 1/8: $t_{1/8} = \frac{\ln 8}{k} = \frac{3\ln 2}{k}$
For reduction to 1/10: $t_{1/10} = \frac{\ln 10}{k}$
Therefore: $\frac{t_{1/8}}{t_{1/10}} = \frac{\ln 8}{\ln 10} = \frac{3\log 2}{\log 10} = \frac{3 \times 0.3}{1} = 0.9$
Thus: $\frac{t_{1/8}}{t_{1/10}} \times 10 = 0.9 \times 10 = 9$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The half-life of ${ }^{65} \mathrm{Zn}$ is 245 days. After $x$ days, $75 \%$ of original activity remained. The value of $x$ in days is $\_\_\_\_$. (Nearest integer)
(Given: $\log 3=0.4771$ and $\log 2=0.3010$)
questions.solution:
Using radioactive decay: $A = A_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/t_{1/2}}$.
With 75% activity remaining: $0.75 = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x/245}$.
Taking log base 10: $\log(0.75) = \frac{x}{245}\log(0.5)$.
Calculate: $\log(0.75) = \log 3 - \log 4 = 0.4771 - 2(0.3010) = -0.1249$ and $\log(0.5) = -0.3010$.
Thus $-0.1249 = \frac{x}{245} \times (-0.3010)$, giving $x = \frac{0.1249 \times 245}{0.3010} = 101.66 \approx 102$ days (nearest integer).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}  in presence of a catalyst, activation energy of a reaction is lowered by $10 $\mathrm{ kJ} $\mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$. The logarithm of ratio of $\frac{$\mathrm{k} \text{ (catalysed) }$}{$\mathrm{k} $\text{ (uncatalysed) }$}$ is....  (Consider that the frequency factor for both the reactions is same)
questions.solution:
Using the Arrhenius equation: $k = A e^{-E_a/RT}$
The ratio of rate constants is: $\frac{k_{catalysed}}{k_{uncatalysed}} = \frac{A e^{-E_a^c/RT}}{A e^{-E_a^u/RT}} = e^{(E_a^u - E_a^c)/RT} = e^{\Delta E_a/RT}$
Since the catalyst lowers activation energy by 10 kJ/mol: $\Delta E_a = 10$ kJ/mol = 10000 J/mol
At T = 27°C = 300 K, R = 8.314 J/(mol·K):
$\frac{k_c}{k_u} = e^{10000/(8.314 \times 300)} = e^{10000/2494.2} = e^{4.009}$
Taking logarithm base 10: $\log_{10}\frac{k_c}{k_u} = 4.009 \times \log_{10}(e) = 4.009 \times 0.4343 = 1.741$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Observe the following reactions at $\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{K})$.
I. $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow$ products.
II. $5 \mathrm{Br}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{BrO}_{3}{ }^{-}(\mathrm{aq})+6 \mathrm{H}^{+}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow 3 \mathrm{Br}_{2}(\mathrm{aq})+3 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})$
Both the reactions are started at 10.00 am. The rates of these reactions at 10.10 am are same. The value of $-\frac{\Delta\left[\mathrm{Br}^{-}\right]}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}$ at 10.10 am is $2 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1} \mathrm{~min}^{-1}$. The concentration of A at 10.10 am is $10^{-2} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$. What is the first order rate constant (in $\mathrm{min}^{-1}$) of reaction $I$ ?
questions.solution:
For reaction II:
5Br$^-$ + BrO$_3^-$ + 6H$^+$\rightarrow$ 3Br$_2$ + 3H$_2$O,
The overall reaction rate is:
$r = -\frac{1}{5}\frac{\Delta[Br^-]}{\Delta t} = -\frac{1}{3}\frac{\Delta[Br_2]}{\Delta t}$.
Given $\frac{\Delta[Br^-]}{\Delta t} = 2 \times 10^{-4}$ mol L$^{-1}$ min$^{-1}$
The reaction rate is $r = \frac{2 \times 10^{-4}}{5} = 4 \times 10^{-5}$ mol L$^{-1}$ min$^{-1}$.
Since the rates of both reactions are equal at 10.10 am and reaction I is first-order:
$r = k[A]$, so $4 \times 10^{-5} = k \times 10^{-2}$, giving $k = 4 \times 10^{-3}$ min$^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Correct statements regarding Arrhenius equation among the following are :
A. Factor $e^{-E a / R T}$ corresponds to fraction of molecules having kinetic energy less than Ea.
B. At a given temperature, lower the Ea, faster is the reaction.
C. Increase in temperature by about $10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ doubles the rate of reaction.
D. Plot of $\log \mathrm{k}$ vs $\frac{1}{\mathrm{~T}}$ gives a straight line with slope $=-\frac{E a}{R}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
The Arrhenius equation is given by $k = A e^{-E_a/RT}$.
Statement A: The factor $e^{-E_a/RT}$ represents the fraction of molecules having kinetic energy equal to or greater than the activation energy $E_a$. Thus, statement A is incorrect.
Statement B: From the equation, as $E_a$ decreases, the value of $k$ increases, leading to a faster reaction rate. Thus, statement B is correct.
Statement C: For many reactions, the temperature coefficient is approximately 2, meaning the rate of reaction doubles for every $10^{\circ}C$ rise in temperature. Thus, statement C is correct.
Statement D: Taking the natural logarithm of the Arrhenius equation, $\ln k = \ln A - \frac{E_a}{RT}$. Converting to base 10, $\log k = \log A - \frac{E_a}{2.303RT}$. A plot of $\log k$ vs $\frac{1}{T}$ gives a straight line with slope $= -\frac{E_a}{2.303R}$. The statement says slope $= -\frac{E_a}{R}$, which is only true for a $\ln k$ vs $\frac{1}{T}$ plot. Thus, statement D is incorrect.
Therefore, statements B and C are correct.
questions.question:
Correct statements regarding Arrhenius equation among the following are :
A. Factor $e^{-E a / R T}$ corresponds to fraction of molecules having kinetic energy less than Ea.
B. At a given temperature, lower the Ea, faster is the reaction.
C. Increase in temperature by about $10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ doubles the rate of reaction.
D. Plot of $\log \mathrm{k}$ vs $\frac{1}{\mathrm{~T}}$ gives a straight line with slope $=-\frac{E a}{R}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation:
The Arrhenius equation is given by $k = A e^{-E_a/RT}$.
Statement A: The factor $e^{-E_a/RT}$ represents the fraction of molecules having kinetic energy equal to or greater than the activation energy $E_a$. Thus, statement A is incorrect.
Statement B: From the equation, as $E_a$ decreases, the value of $k$ increases, leading to a faster reaction rate. Thus, statement B is correct.
Statement C: For many reactions, the temperature coefficient is approximately 2, meaning the rate of reaction doubles for every $10^{\circ}C$ rise in temperature. Thus, statement C is correct.
Statement D: Taking the natural logarithm of the Arrhenius equation, $\ln k = \ln A - \frac{E_a}{RT}$. Converting to base 10, $\log k = \log A - \frac{E_a}{2.303RT}$. A plot of $\log k$ vs $\frac{1}{T}$ gives a straight line with slope $= -\frac{E_a}{2.303R}$. The statement says slope $= -\frac{E_a}{R}$, which is only true for a $\ln k$ vs $\frac{1}{T}$ plot. Thus, statement D is incorrect.
Therefore, statements B and C are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider $\mathrm{A} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{k}_{1}} \mathrm{~B}$ and $\mathrm{C} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{k}_{2}} \mathrm{D}$ are two reactions. If the rate constant $\left(\mathrm{k}_{1}\right)$ of the $\mathrm{A} \longrightarrow \mathrm{B}$ reaction can be expressed by the following equation $\log _{10} \mathrm{k}=14.34-\frac{1.5 \times 10^{4}}{\mathrm{~T} / \mathrm{K}}$ and activation energy of $C \longrightarrow D$ reaction $\left(E a_{2}\right)$ is $\frac{1}{5}$ th of the $A \longrightarrow B$ reaction $\left(E a_{1}\right)$, then the value of $\left(E a_{2}\right)$ is $\_\_\_\_ \mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest Integer)
questions.solution:
From the Arrhenius equation:
$\log_{10} k = \log_{10} A - \frac{E_a}{2.303RT}$.
Comparing with given equation $\log_{10} k_1 = 14.34 - \frac{1.5 \times 10^4}{T}$, we get: $\frac{E_{a_1}}{2.303R} = 1.5 \times 10^4$ K

$E_{a_1} = 1.5 \times 10^4 \times 2.303 \times 8.314$
$= 1.5 \times 10^4 \times 0.01913$
$= 287$ kJ/mol

Since $E_{a_2} = \frac{1}{5} E_{a_1}$:

$E_{a_2} = \frac{287}{5} = 57.4 \approx 57$ kJ/mol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$\mathrm{A} \rightarrow$ product (First order reaction). Three sets of experiment were performed for a reaction under similar experimental conditions:
Run $1 \Rightarrow 100 \mathrm{~mL}$ of 10 M solution of reactant A
Run $2 \Rightarrow 200 \mathrm{~mL}$ of 10 M solution of reactant A
Run $3 \Rightarrow 100 \mathrm{~mL}$ of 10 M solution of reactant $\mathrm{A}+100 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$ added.
The correct variation of rate of reaction is
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, rate = $k[A]$, where rate is directly proportional to reactant concentration.
Run 1: 100 mL of 10 M solution
Concentration = 10 M
Rate: $r_1 = k \times 10$
Run 2: 200 mL of 10 M solution
Concentration remains 10 M (increasing volume doesn't change concentration)
Rate: $r_2 = k \times 10$
Therefore $r_1 = r_2$
Run 3: 100 mL of 10 M solution + 100 mL of H₂O
Total moles of A = 10 M × 0.1 L = 1 mol
Total volume = 0.2 L
New concentration = 1 mol / 0.2 L = 5 M
Rate: $r_3 = k \times 5$
Therefore $r_3 < r_1 = r_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The temperature at which the rate constants of the given below two gaseous reactions become equal is $\_\_\_\_$ K. (Nearest integer)
$\mathrm{X} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Y} \quad \mathrm{k}_{1}=10^{6} e^{\frac{-30000}{\mathrm{~T}}}$
$\mathrm{P} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Q} \quad \mathrm{k}_{2}=10^{4} e^{\frac{-24000}{\mathrm{~T}}}$
Given: $\ln 10=2.303$
questions.solution:
To find the temperature at which $k_1 = k_2$,
set the rate constant equations equal: $10^6 e^{-30000/T} = 10^4 e^{-24000/T}$.
Dividing both sides by $10^4$: $100 = e^{-24000/T + 30000/T} = e^{6000/T}$.
Taking natural logarithm: $\ln(100) = \frac{6000}{T}$.
Since $\ln(100) = 2\ln(10) = 2 \times 2.303 = 4.606$: $4.606 = \frac{6000}{T}$.
Solving for T: $T = \frac{6000}{4.606} = 1302.5$ K.
Rounding to the nearest integer gives T = 1303 K.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Decomposition of A is a first order reaction at $\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{K})$ and is given by $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{B}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g})$. In a closed 1 L vessel, 1 bar $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g})$ is allowed to decompose at $\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{K})$. After 100 minutes, the total pressure was 1.5 bar. What is the rate constant $\left(\mathrm{in} \mathrm{min}^{-1}\right)$ of the reaction ? $(\log 2=0.3)$
questions.solution:
For the reaction $A(g) \rightarrow B(g) + C(g)$, initially pressure of A is 1 bar.
Initially: total pressure = 1 bar.
After 100 min: total pressure = 1.5 bar.
Using initial and final pressures, if x bar of A decomposes, then A becomes (1-x), B = x, C = x.
Total pressure = 1-x+x+x = 1+x = 1.5, so x = 0.5 bar.
For a first-order reaction: $k = \frac{2.303}{t} \log \frac{[A]_0}{[A]}$.
Using pressures instead: $k = \frac{2.303}{100} \log \frac{1}{0.5}$
$=\frac{2.303}{100} \times \log 2 = \frac{2.303 \times 0.3}{100} = \frac{0.691}{100}$
$= 6.91 \times 10^{-3}$ min$^{-1}$ ≈ $6.9 \times 10^{-3}$ min$^{-1}$

questions.q: Pre-exponential factors of two different reactions of same order are identical. Let activation energy of first reaction exceeds the activation energy of second reaction by $20 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$. If $\mathrm{k}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{k}_{2}$ are the rate constants of first and second reaction respectively at 300 K, then $\ln \frac{\mathrm{k}_{2}}{\mathrm{k}_{1}}$ will be $\_\_\_\_$. (nearest integer) $\left[\mathrm{R}=8.3 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right]$
questions.solution:
Given: $A_1 = A_2$, $E_{a1} = E_{a2} + 20$ kJ/mol, T = 300 K, R = 8.3 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹
Using Arrhenius equation: $k = Ae^{-E_a/RT}$
$\frac{k_2}{k_1} = \frac{e^{-E_{a2}/RT}}{e^{-E_{a1}/RT}} = e^{(E_{a1} - E_{a2})/RT}$
$E_{a1} - E_{a2} = 20$ kJ/mol = 20000 J/mol
$\frac{k_2}{k_1} = e^{\frac{20000}{8.3 \times 300}} = e^{\frac{20000}{2490}}$
$\ln\frac{k_2}{k_1} = \frac{20000}{2490} = 8.03 \approx 8$

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}}$ for forward and backward reaction are 180 and $200 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ respectively
If catalyst lowers $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}}$ for both reaction by $100 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$.
Which of the following statement is correct?
options: Catalyst does not alter the Gibbs energy change of a reaction.
Catalyst can cause non-spontaneous reactions to occur.

The enthalpy change for the catalysed reaction is different from that of uncatalysed reaction.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{A}_2+\mathrm{B}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{AB}$
$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{f}}=180 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$

$\Delta \mathrm{H}=\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{b}}=-20 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$

$\begin{aligned}

& \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{b}}=200-100=100 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$
Catalyst does not change $\Delta \mathrm{H}$ or $\Delta \mathrm{G}$ of a reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a reaction $A+B \rightarrow C$, initial concentrations of $A$ and $B$ are related as $[A]_0=8[B]_0$. The half lives of $A$ and $B$ are 10 min and 40 min. respectively. If they start to disappear at the same time, both following first order kinetics, after how much time will the concentration of both the reactants be same?
questions.solution:
Given : $[\mathrm{A}]_0=8[\mathrm{~B}]_0$
$\left[\mathrm{t}_{1 / 2}\right]_{\mathrm{A}}=10 \mathrm{~min}$.
$\left[\mathrm{t}_{1 / 2}\right]_{\mathrm{B}}=40 \mathrm{~min}$.
$\mathrm{I}^{\text{st }}$ order kinetics
$\mathrm{t}=$ ?
$[\mathrm{A}]_{\mathrm{t}}=[\mathrm{B}]_{\mathrm{t}}$
$-\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{A}} \times \mathrm{t} \quad-\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{B}} \times \mathrm{t}$
$\Rightarrow \quad[\mathrm{A}]_0 \mathrm{e}=[\mathrm{B}]_0 \mathrm{e}$
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{[\mathrm{A}]_0}{[\mathrm{~B}]_0}=\mathrm{e}^{\left(\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{A}}-\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{B}}\right) \mathrm{t}}$
$\Rightarrow \quad 8=\mathrm{e}^{\left(\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{A}}-\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{B}}\right) \times \mathrm{t}}$
$\Rightarrow \quad \ell \mathrm{n} 8=\left(\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{A}}-\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{B}}\right) \times \mathrm{t}$
$\Rightarrow \quad \ln 8=\ln 2\left(\frac{1}{\left(\operatorname{ta}_2\right)_{\mathrm{A}}}-\frac{1}{\left(\operatorname{ta}_2\right)_{\mathrm{B}}}\right) \times \mathrm{t}$

questions.q: The reaction \(\mathrm{A}_2+\mathrm{B}_2 \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{AB}\) follows the mechanism The overall order of the reaction is :
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ rate }=\mathrm{k}_2[\mathrm{ A}]\left[\mathrm{B}_2\right] \ldots \ldots \\
& \left(\frac{\mathrm{k}_1}{\mathrm{k}_{-1}}\right)=\left(\frac{[\mathrm{A}]^2}{\left[\mathrm{ A}_2\right]}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow[\mathrm{A}]=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{k}_1}{\mathrm{k}_{-1}}} \cdot \sqrt{\left[\mathrm{ A}_2\right]}
\end{aligned}$

Substituting in (1) ; we get


$\begin{aligned} & \text{ Rate }=\mathrm{k}_2 \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{k}_1}{\mathrm{k}_{-1}}} \cdot\left[\mathrm{ A}_2\right]^{\frac{1}{2}} \cdot\left[\mathrm{ B}_2\right] \\ & \therefore \text{ order }=\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)=1.5\end{aligned}$

$\frac{t_1}{2} \propto\left(C_0\right)^{1-\eta}$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{t_1}{t_2}=\left(\frac{C_1}{C_2}\right)^{1-\eta} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{200}{100}=\left(\frac{0.100}{0.025}\right)^{1-\eta} \\
& \Rightarrow 2=(4)^{1-\eta} \\
& (1-\eta)=\frac{1}{2} \\
& \eta=\frac{1}{2} \\
& \text{ For } \eta=\frac{1}{2} \\
& \frac{-d A}{d t}=k(A)^{\frac{1}{2}} \\
& \int_{C_0}^C \frac{d A}{(A)^{\frac{1}{2}}}=-\int_0^t k d t \\
& \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{~A}^{\frac{1}{2}}=-\mathrm{kt} \\
& \Rightarrow \sqrt{\mathrm{C}}-\sqrt{\mathrm{C}_0}=\frac{-\mathrm{kt}}{2} \\
& \sqrt{\mathrm{C}}-\sqrt{\mathrm{C}_0}-\frac{\mathrm{kt}}{2} \\
& \text{ For } \mathrm{C}_0=0.1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}_{\frac{1}{2}}=200 \mathrm{~min} \\
& \sqrt{\frac{c_0}{2}}=\sqrt{c_0}-\frac{k t}{2} \\
& \frac{\mathrm{kt}}{2}=\sqrt{\mathrm{c}_0}-\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{c}_0}{2}} \\
& \frac{\mathrm{kt}}{2}=\sqrt{\mathrm{c}_0}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \\
& t_{\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{2 \sqrt{c_0}}{k}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \\
& 200=\frac{2 \sqrt{0.1}}{k}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)
\end{aligned}$\mathrm{k}=\frac{\sqrt{0.1}}{100}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider a complex reaction taking place in three steps with rate constants $k_1, k_2$ and $k_3$ respectively. The overall rate constant $k$ is given by the expression $k=\sqrt{\frac{k_1 k_3}{k_2}}$. If the activation energies of the three steps are 60,30 and $10 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}{ }^{-1}$ respectively, then the overall energy of activation in $\mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ is $\ldots\ldots$ . (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{k}_1, \mathrm{k}_2$ and $\mathrm{k}_3$ are given as rate constants of three steps of a complex reaction. Rate constant (k) of the overall reaction is given as
$k=\sqrt{\frac{k_1 k_3}{k_2}}$
Activation energies of the three steps are given as
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_1}=60 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}, \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_2}=30 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}, \\
& \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_3}=10 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$
From Arrhenius equation, we know that
$\mathrm{k}=\mathrm{Ae}^{-\mathrm{Ea} / \mathrm{RT} T}$
If $E_a$ is the activation energy of the overall reaction, then
$\begin{aligned}
& E_a=\frac{1}{2}\left[E_{a_1}+E_{a_3}-E_{a_2}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{2}[60+10-30]=20 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
$\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{~B}$
The molecule A changes into its isomeric form B by following a first order kinetics at a temperature of 1000 K . If the energy barrier with respect to reactant energy for such isomeric transformation is $191.48 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ and the frequency factor is $10^{20}$, the time required for $50 \%$ molecules of A to become $B$ is _________ picoseconds (nearest integer). $\left[\mathrm{R}=8.314 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right]$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{t}_{1 / 2}=\frac{0.693}{\mathrm{~K}} \\ & \mathrm{~K}=\mathrm{Ae}^{-\mathrm{Ea} / \mathrm{RT}} \\ & =10^{20} \times \mathrm{e}^{-\frac{191.48 \times 10^3}{8.314 \times 1000}} \\ & =10^{20} \times \mathrm{e}^{-23.031}=10^{20} \times-\mathrm{e}^{\ln 10 \times 10} \\ & =\frac{10^{20}}{10^{10}}=10^{10} \mathrm{sec} . \\ & \mathrm{t}_{1 / 2}=\frac{0.693}{10^{10}}=6.93 \times 10^{-11} \\ & \quad=69.3 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{sec} .\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{~B}(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g}) \\ & \mathrm{P}_{23}=\mathrm{P}_0+2 \mathrm{x}=200 \\ & \mathrm{P}_{\infty}=3 \mathrm{P}_0=300 \\ & \mathrm{P}_0=100 \\ & \mathrm{~K}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}} \ln \frac{\mathrm{P}_{\infty}-\mathrm{P}_0}{\mathrm{P}_{\infty}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{t}}} \\ & \mathrm{K}=\frac{2.3}{23} \log \frac{300-100}{300-200} \\ & =\frac{2.3 \times 0.301}{23}=0.0301=3.01 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{sec}^{-1} \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Consider the following single step reaction in gas phase at constant temperature.
\(2 $\mathrm{~A}_{(\mathrm{g})}+\mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_{(\mathrm{g})}$\)
The initial rate of the reaction is recorded as \($\mathrm{r}}_{1}\) when the reaction starts with \(1.5  \mathrm{~atm}\) pressure of \($\mathrm{A}$\) and \(0.7  \mathrm{~atm}\) pressure of \($\mathrm{B}$\). After some time, the rate \( \mathrm{r}$}_{2}\) is recorded when the pressure of \($\mathrm{C}$\) becomes \(0.5 $\mathrm{~atm}$\). The ratio \($\mathrm{r}}_{1}:  \mathrm{r}$}_{2}\) is ______ \($\times$10^{-1}\). (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
$2 \mathrm{~A}(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{g}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g})$
$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{r}_1 & 1.5 \mathrm{~atm} \quad 0.7 \mathrm{~atm} \\ \mathrm{r}_2 & 0.5 \mathrm{~atm} \quad 0.2 \mathrm{~atm} \quad 0.5 \mathrm{~atm} \\ & \because \mathrm{r}=\mathrm{K}\left[\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}\right]^2\left[\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}\right] \\ & \mathrm{r}_1=\mathrm{K}[1.5]^2[0.7] \\ & \mathrm{r}_2=\mathrm{K}[0.5]^2[0.2] \\ & \frac{\mathrm{r}_1}{\mathrm{r}_2}=9 \times \frac{7}{2}=31.5=315 \times 10^{-1} \end{array}$ Ans. 315

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
During Kinetic study of reaction \(2 A+B \rightarrow C+D\), the following results were obtained :
\(\begin{array}{llll} 
& \text{ A [M] } & \text{ B [M] } & \text{ initial rate of formation of D } \\
\text{ I } & 0.1 & 0.1 & 6.0 \times 10^{-3} \\
\text{ II } & 0.3 & 0.2 & 7.20 \times 10^{-2} \\
\text{ III } & 0.3 & 0.4 & 2.88 \times 10^{-1} \\
\text{ IV } & 0.4 & 0.1 & 2.40 \times 10^{-2} \\
\end{array}\)
Based on above data, overall order of the reaction is ______
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{r}=\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{A}]^{\mathrm{x}}[\mathrm{B}]^{\mathrm{y}} \\ & (\mathrm{I}) 6 \times 10^{-3}=\mathrm{K}[0.1]^{\mathrm{x}}[0.1]^{\mathrm{y}} \\ & (\mathrm{IV}) 2.4 \times 10^{-2}=\mathrm{K}[0.4]^{\mathrm{x}}[0.1]^{\mathrm{y}} \\ & \quad(\mathrm{IV}) /(\mathrm{I}) \\ & 4=(4)^{\mathrm{x}} \\ & \quad \mathrm{x}=1 \\ & \mathrm{r}=\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{A}]^{\mathrm{x}}[\mathrm{B}]^{\mathrm{y}}\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & \text{ (III) } 2.88 \times 10^{-1}=\mathrm{K}[0.3]^{\mathrm{x}}[0.4]^{\mathrm{y}} \\ & \text{ (II) } 7.2 \times 10^{-2}=\mathrm{K}[0.3]^{\mathrm{x}}[0.2]^{\mathrm{y}} \\ & \text{ (III)/(II) }\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & 4=2^y \\ & y=2\end{aligned}$
Overall order $=x+y=1+2=3$

questions.q:
Consider the following transformation involving first order elementary reaction in each step at constant temperature as shown below.
\(A+B \underset{\text{ Step 3 }}{\text{ Step } 1} C \xrightarrow{\text{ Step 2 }} P\)
Some details of the above reactions are listed below.
\($\begin{array}{ccc}
\text{ Step } & \text{ Rate constant }\left(\mathbf{s e c}^{-\mathbf{1}}\right) & \text{ Activation energy }\left(\mathbf{k J ~ m o l}^{-\mathbf{1}}\right) \\
1 & \mathrm{k}_1 & 300 \\
2 & \mathrm{k}_2 & 200 \\
3 & \mathrm{k}_3 & \mathrm{Ea}_3
\end{array}$
If the overall rate constant of the above transformation \((k)\) is given as \(k=\frac{k_1 k_2}{k_3}\) and the overall activation energy \(\left(\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}}\right)\) is \(400 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\), then the value of \(\mathrm{Ea}_3\) is \(\qquad\) \(\mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}\) (nearest integer)
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{K}=\frac{\mathrm{K}_1 \mathrm{~K}_2}{\mathrm{~K}_3} \\ & \mathrm{Ae}^{\frac{-\mathrm{E}_3}{\mathrm{RT}}}=\frac{\mathrm{A}_1 \mathrm{e}^{\frac{-\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_1}}{\mathrm{RT}}} \mathrm{A}_2 \mathrm{e}^{\frac{-\mathrm{E}_{3_2}}{\mathrm{RT}}}}{\mathrm{A}_3 \mathrm{e}^{\frac{-\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{k}_3}}{\mathrm{RT}}}} \\ & \mathrm{Ae}^{\frac{-\mathrm{E}_3}{\mathrm{RT}}}=\frac{\mathrm{A}_1 \mathrm{~A}_2}{\mathrm{~A}_3} \mathrm{e}^{\frac{-\left(\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_1}-\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_2}-\mathrm{E}_{3_3}\right)}{\mathrm{RT}}} \\ & \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}}=\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_1}+\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_2}-\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_3} \\ & 400=300+200-\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_3} \\ & \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_3}=100 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mole}\end{aligned}$

$- \dfrac{\Delta\left[{N}_{2}{O}_{5}\right]}{\Delta t} = - \dfrac{( 2 . 75 - 3 )}{30 - 0}mol{L}^{- 1}{min}^{- 1} = \dfrac{0 . 25}{30}$

questions.q: For a reaction taking place in three steps at same temperature, overall rate constant $K = \dfrac{{K}_{1}{K}_{2}}{{K}_{3}}$. If ${Ea}_{1}, {Ea}_{2}$ and ${Ea}_{3}$ are $40, 50$ and $60kJ / mol$ respectively, the overall $Ea$ is _________ $kJ / mol$.
questions.solution:
According to Arrhenius concept,

$K = {Ae}^{- {E}_{a} / RT}$

Given that,

${K}_{} = \left({K}_{1} . {K}_{2}\right) / {K}_{3}$

Using Arrhenius equation we can expand above equation as

${e}^{- {E}_{a ( net )} / RT} = \dfrac{{e}^{- {E}_{a1} / RT} \times {e}^{- {E}_{a2} / RT}}{{e}^{- {E}_{a3} / RT}}$

Hence,

 ${E}_{a ( net )} = {E}_{a1} + {E}_{a2} - {E}_{a3} ⇒ {E}_{a ( net )} = 40 + 50 - 60 = 30kJ / mol$

questions.q: For a reversible reaction $A ⇌ B$, the $∆ H$ forward reaction $= 20kJ{mol}^{– 1}$. The activation energy of the uncatalyzed forward reaction is $300kJ{mol}^{– 1}$. When the reaction is catalysed keeping the reactant concentration same, the rate of the catalysed forward reaction at ${27}^{∘}C$ is found to be same as that of the uncatalyzed reaction at ${327}^{∘}C$. The activation energy of the catalysed backward reaction is _______$kJ{mol}^{– 1}$.
questions.solution:
As per the question

To determine the activation energy of the catalyzed backward reaction, we need to use the Arrhenius equation and the given information.

The Arrhenius equation is given by:

$k = {Ae}^{( - Ea / RT )}$

${Ae}^{- \dfrac{300 \times {10}^{3}}{600 \times R}} = Ae\dfrac{- Ea}{300 \times R}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{10}^{3}}{2} = \dfrac{Ea}{300}$

$⇒ {E}_{a} = 150 \times {10}^{3}J{mol}^{– 1}$

$⇒ {E}_{a} = 150kJ{mol}^{– 1}$

$∴$ Activation energy of catalysed backward reaction

Energy of activation for backward reaction${E}_{b} = {E}_{a} - ∆ H$

$= 150 - 20 = 130kJ{mol}^{– 1}$

questions.q:
The reaction $2NO + {Br}_{2} \to 2NOBr$ takes place through the mechanism given below

$NO + {Br}_{2}⇌{NOBr}_{2}\left(fast\right)$

${NOBr}_{2} + NO \to 2NOBr\left(slow\right)$

The overall order of the reaction is _____.
questions.solution:
On applying Law of mass action over slowest step,

$R = k [ {NOBr}_{2} ] [ NO ]$

The slowest step is the rate determining step.

On applying Law of mass action on equilibrium of Step I

$k = \dfrac{\left[{NOBr}_{2}\right]}{\left[NO\right]\left[{Br}_{2}\right]}$

$\left[{NOBr}_{2}\right] = k\left[NO\right]\left[{Br}_{2}\right]$

Hence, overall rate equation will be

$R = k{\left[NO\right]}^{2}\left[{Br}_{2}\right]$

$= k ' {\left[NO\right]}^{2}\left[{Br}_{2}\right]$

The overall order is equal to sum of the powers of the concentration terms in the rate law.

The overall order of the reaction is 3.

${NOBr}_{2} + NO \to 2NOBr\left(slow\right)$

The slowest step is the rate determining step.

The overall order is equal to sum of the powers of the concentration terms in the rate law.

The overall order of the reaction is 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A molecule undergoes two independent first order reactions whose respective half lives are $12min$ and $3min$. If both the reactions are occurring then the time taken for the $50 %$ consumption of the reactant is ______ $min$. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
For parallel reaction

When adding the rate constants of the two reactions, we need to use the formula for combining rate constants of two reactions in parallel, which is:

$k = {k}_{1} + {k}_{2}$

where ${k}_{1}$ and ${k}_{2}$ are the rate constants of the individual reactions.

In this case, the half-lives of the two reactions are $12$ min and $3$ min, respectively. The rate constants of the two reactions can be calculated using the formula for half-life of a first-order reaction:

$\dfrac{1}{{t}_{1 / 2}} = \dfrac{1}{12} + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{5}{12}$

Net ${t}_{1 / 2} = \dfrac{12}{5} = 2 . 4min \approx 2min$

Hence time taken for $50 %$ consumption of reactant will be close to $2min$.

questions.q:
The number of given statement/s which is/are correct is_____

(A) The stronger the temperature dependence of the rate constant, the higher is the activation energy.

(B) If a reaction has zero activation energy, its rate is independent of temperature.

(C) The stronger the temperature dependence of the rate constant, the smaller is the activation energy.

(D) If there is no correlation between the temperature and the rate constant then it means that the reaction has negative activation energy.
questions.solution:
Rate constant is given by Arrhenius equation

$k = {Ae}^{- {E}_{a} / RT}$

Higher the magnitude of activation energy, stronger is the temperature dependence of the rate constant. The pre-exponential factor is a measure of the rate at which collisions occur, irrespective of their energy. If the activation energy of reaction is zero, temperature will have no effect on the rate constant.

questions.q: A and B are two substances undergoing radioactive decay in a container. The half life of A is $15min$ and that of B is $5min$. If the initial concentration of B is $4$ times that of A and they both start decaying at the same time, how much time will it take for the concentration of both of them to be same? ________min.
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction:
$⇒ [ A{]}_{t} = [ A{]}_{0}{e}^{- kt}$

For $A$ : Let $[ A{]}_{t}$ be $y$ and $[ A{]}_{0}$ be x
For a first order reaction:
$∴ k = \dfrac{ln2}{{t}_{1 / 2}} = \dfrac{ln2}{15min}$

$⇒ y = {xe}^{- kt}$

$= {xe}^{- \left(\dfrac{ln2}{15}\right)t}$ ....(1)

Similarly For B:
$[ B{]}_{t} = [ B{]}_{0}{e}^{- kt}$

Let $[ B{]}_{t} = y; [ B{]}_{0} = 4x; k = \dfrac{ln2}{{t}_{1 / 2}} = \dfrac{ln2}{5min}$

$⇒ y = 4{xe}^{- \left(\dfrac{ln2}{5}\right)t}$ ....(2)
Equating equation(1) and (2) we get:

$⇒ {xe}^{- \left(\dfrac{ln2}{15}\right)t} = 4{xe}^{- \left(\dfrac{ln2}{5}\right)t}$

$⇒ t \times \left[\dfrac{ln2}{5} - \dfrac{ln2}{15}\right] = ln4$

$⇒ t \times ln2\left[\dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{15}\right] = 2ln2$

$⇒ {e}^{t\left(\dfrac{ln2}{5} - \dfrac{ln2}{15}\right)} = 4$

$⇒ t = 15min$

$A \to B$

The rate constants of the above reaction at $200K$ and $300K$ are $0 . 03{min}^{- 1}$ and $0 . 05{min}^{- 1}$ respectively. The activation energy for the reaction is $J$ (Nearest integer)

$R = 8 . 3J{K}^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}$

$log5 = 0 . 70$

$log3 = 0 . 48$

$log2 = 0 . 30$
questions.solution:
If $K$ is known at two different temperatures the activation energy can be calculated as:

At temperature 1: $ln{K}_{1} = - \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{{RT}_{1}} + lnA$

At temperature 2: $ln{K}_{2} = - \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{{RT}_{2}} + lnA$

We can subtract one of these equations from the other:

$ln{K}_{1} - ln{K}_{2} = \left(- \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{{RT}_{1}} + lnA\right) - \left(- \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{{RT}_{2}} + lnA\right)$

This equation can further simplified to:

$ln\dfrac{{K}_{1}}{{K}_{2}} = \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{R}\left(\dfrac{1}{{T}_{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{T}_{1}}\right)$

$ln\dfrac{0 . 05}{0 . 03} = \dfrac{Ea}{2 . 305 \times 8 . 314} \times \left[\dfrac{1}{200} - \dfrac{1}{300}\right]$

$⇒ 0 . 22 = \dfrac{Ea}{2 . 305 \times 8 . 314} \times \left[\dfrac{1}{600}\right]$

$⇒ {E}_{a} = 2 . 3 \times 8 . 3 \times 600 \times 0 . 22$

$⇒ {E}_{a} = 2519 . 88J ⇒ {E}_{a} = 2520J$

Given : $ln10 = 2 . 3; log2 = 0 . 3$
questions.explanation:
For the First order reaction, integrated rate equation can be written as follows,

$t = \dfrac{1}{k}ln\dfrac{{a}_{0}}{{a}_{t}}t = timek = rateconstant{a}_{0} = intialconcentration{a}_{t} = concentrationattimet$

$\dfrac{{t}_{1}}{{t}_{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{k}ln\dfrac{{a}_{0}}{0 . 4{a}_{0}}}{\dfrac{1}{k}ln\dfrac{{a}_{0}}{0 . 1{a}_{0}}}$

$\dfrac{540}{{t}_{2}} = \dfrac{ln\dfrac{10}{4}}{ln10}$

$\dfrac{540}{{t}_{2}} = \dfrac{log10 - log4}{log10}$

$\dfrac{540}{{t}_{2}} = \dfrac{1 - 0 . 6}{1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{540}{{t}_{2}} = 0 . 4$

$⇒ {t}_{2} = \dfrac{540}{0 . 4} = 1350sec$

questions.q: If compound $A$ reacts with $B$ following first order kinetics with rate constant $2 . 011 \times {10}^{- 3}{s}^{- 1}$. The time taken by A (in seconds) to reduce from $7g to 2g$ will be _____ . (Nearest Integer) $\left[log5 = 0 . 698, log7 = 0 . 845, log2 = 0 . 301\right]$
questions.solution:
Given,
$\begin{cases} & & A + B \to P \\ t = 0 & & 7g \\ t = t & & 2g\end{cases}$

at constant volume

From formula of first order kinetics:
$⇒ t = \dfrac{2 . 303}{K}log\dfrac{{\left[A\right]}_{0}}{{\left[A\right]}_{t}}$

$= \dfrac{2 \cdot 303}{2 \cdot 011 \times {10}^{- 3}}log\dfrac{7}{2}$

$= \dfrac{2 \cdot 303 \times 0 . 544}{2 \cdot 011 \times {10}^{- 3}}$

$= 622 . 989$

$\approx 623$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For conversion of compound $A \to B$, the rate constant of the reaction was found to be $4 . 6 \times {10}^{- 5}Lmol - 1 {s}^{- 1}$. The order of the reaction is _____ .
questions.solution:
Rate(r) $= k{\left[A\right]}^{n}$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{rate}{{\left[A\right]}^{n}}$

Unit of rate constant is related to order of reaction$( n )$ by the relation: ${\left(conc .\right)}^{1 - n}{time}^{- 1}$

Thus,
$\begin{array}{ll}⇒ \left({Lmol}^{- 1}\right) ⇒ 1 - n = - 1 \\ n = 2\end{array}$

questions.q:
A first order reaction has the rate constant, $k = 4 . 6 \times {10}^{- 3}{s}^{- 1}$. The number of correct statement/s from the following is/are Given: $log3 = 0 . 48$.

A. Reaction completes in $1000s$.
B. The reaction has a half-life of $500s$.
C. The time required for $10 %$ completion is 25 times the time required for 90% completion.
D. The degree of dissociation is equal to $\left(1 - {e}^{- kt}\right)$.
E. The rate and the rate constant have the same unit.
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction:
$t\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{0 . 693}{k} = \dfrac{0 . 693}{4 . 6 \times {10}^{- 3}{s}^{- 1}} = 150 . 65s$

For a first order reaction,
${t}_{10 %} = \dfrac{1}{K}ln\left(\dfrac{a}{a - x}\right) = \dfrac{1}{K}ln\left(\dfrac{100}{90}\right)$

${t}_{10 %} = \dfrac{2 . 303}{K} ( log10 - log9 )$

${t}_{10 %} = \dfrac{2 . 093}{K} \times ( 0 . 04 )$


Similarly

${t}_{90 %} = \dfrac{1}{K}ln\left(\dfrac{100}{10}\right)$

${t}_{90 %} = \dfrac{2 . 303}{K}$

$\dfrac{{t}_{90 %}}{{t}_{10 %}} = \dfrac{1}{0 . 04} = 25$


We know,
${e}^{kt} = \dfrac{a}{a - x}$

$\dfrac{a - x}{a} = {e}^{- kt}$

$x = a\left(1 - {e}^{- kt}\right)$

$\alpha = \dfrac{x}{a} = \left(1 - {e}^{- kt}\right)$

Thus, only option (D) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A student has studied the decomposition of a gas $A{B}_{3}$ at $25 ° C$. He obtained the following data

$p ( mmHg )$ $50$ $100$ $200$ $400$
Relative $t\dfrac{1}{2}\left(s\right)$ $4$ $2$ $1$ $0 . 5$

The order of the reaction is
questions.solution:
By observing the data given, by doubling the pressure, half-life is reduced to half. This result is following second order kinetics. Mathematically it can be proved as follows,

The half-life and initial pressure of ${n}^{th}$ order reaction can be related as follows,

$t\dfrac{1}{2} ∝ {\left({P}_{o}\right)}^{1 - n}$

$\dfrac{{\left({t}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}\right)}_{1}}{{\left(t\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}_{2}} = {\left({P}_{0}\right)}_{1}^{1 - n}{\left({P}_{0}\right)}_{2}^{1 - n}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{4}{2}\right) = {\left(\dfrac{50}{100}\right)}^{1 - n}$

$⇒ 2 = {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{1 - n}$

$⇒ 2 = {\left(2\right)}^{n - 1}$

$⇒ n - 1 = 1$

$⇒ n = 2$

Hence, the order of the reaction is second order.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The number of correct statement/s from the following is _____ .

A.Larger the activation energy, smaller is the value of the rate constant.

B. The higher is the activation energy, higher is the value of the temperature coefficient.

C. At lower temperatures, increase in temperature causes more change in the value of $k$ than at higher temperature.

D. A plot of $lnk$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$ is a straight line with slope equal to $- \dfrac{Ea}{R}$
questions.solution:
$A: k = {Ae}^{- \dfrac{Ea}{RT}}$(Arrhenius rate equation)

As $Ea$(Activation energy) increases $k$(rate constant) decreases

B :Higher activation energy, greater is the effect of given temperature rise on rate constant 'k'. Activation energy is the minimum energy needed for the reaction to occur. When temperature increases, Kinetic Energy also increases; as temperature increases, more molecules have higher Kinetic Energy, and thus the fraction of molecules that have high enough Kinetic Energy to overcome the energy barrier also increases.

Temperature coefficient $= \dfrac{{k}_{T + 10}}{{k}_{T}}$

Option (C) is wrong. $\Delta k$ may be greater or lesser depending on temperature.

$D: lnk = lnA - \dfrac{Ea}{RT}$ in this equation the slope is $- \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{R}$.

we know that half life time ${t}_{1 / 2} = \dfrac{ln2}{\lambda}$

The reaction between $X$ and $Y$ is first order with respect to $X$ and zero order with respect to $Y$.

Experiment $\dfrac{\left[X\right]}{{molL}^{- 1}}$ $\dfrac{\left[Y\right]}{{molL}^{- 1}}$ $\dfrac{Initial rate}{mol{L}^{- 1}{min}^{- 1}}$
I $0 . 1$ $0 . 1$ $2 \times {10}^{- 3}$
II $L$ $0 . 2$ $4 \times {10}^{- 3}$
III $0 . 4$ $0 . 4$ $M \times {10}^{- 3}$
IV $0 . 1$ $0 . 2$ $2 \times {10}^{- 3}$

Examine the data of table and calculate ratio of numerical values of $M$ and $L$.
questions.solution:
Given that reaction is first order with respect to X and of zero order with respect to Y.

Means $r = k\left[X\right]{\left[Y\right]}^{0}$ Where k = rate constant.

Using data $I$ & $II$

$\dfrac{4 \times {10}^{- 3}}{2 \times {10}^{- 3}} = \left(\dfrac{L}{0 . 1}\right){\left(\dfrac{0 . 2}{0 . 1}\right)}^{0} ⇒ L = 0 . 2$

Using data from $I$ & $III$

$\dfrac{M \times {10}^{- 3}}{2 \times {10}^{- 3}} = \dfrac{0 . 4}{0 . 1} ⇒ M = 8$

Not the ratio which is asked in question

$\dfrac{M}{L} = \dfrac{8}{0 . 2} = 40$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$2NO + 2{H}_{2} \to {N}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$

The above reaction has been studied at $800 ° C$. The related data are given in the table below

Reaction serial number Initial pressure of${H}_{2} / kPa$ Initial Pressure
of $NO / kPa$		 Initial rate $\left(\dfrac{- dp}{dt}\right) / \left(kPa / s\right)
$1$ $65 . 6$ $40 . 0$ $0 . 135$
$2$ $65 . 6$ $20 . 1$ $0 . 033$
$3$ $38 . 6$ $65 . 6$ $0 . 214$
$4$ $19 . 2$ $65 . 6$ $0 . 106$

The order of the reaction with respect to NO is____

$
questions.solution:
The rate law for the reaction $2NO + 2{H}_{2} \to {N}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$ is

$r = k{\left[{H}_{2}\right]}^{m}{\left[NO\right]}^{n}$

The powers of the concentration terms m, n are the order with respect to hydrogen and nitric oxide respectively.

${E}_{a} = \dfrac{2 . 3 \times 0 . 30 \times 300 \times 309}{9}$

${E}_{a} = 58 . 988 \times {10}^{3}J = 58 . 988kJ = 59kJ$

questions.q: For a given chemical reaction ${\gamma}_{1}A + {\gamma}_{2}B \to {\gamma}_{3}C + {\gamma}_{4}D$. Concentration of $C$ changes from $10mmol{dm}^{- 3}$ to $20mmol{dm}^{- 3}$ in $10s .$ Rate of appearance of $D$ is $1 . 5$ times the rate of disappearance of $B$ which is twice the rate of disappearance $A$. The rate of appearance of $D$ has been experimentally determined to be $9mmol{dm}^{- 3}{s}^{- 1} .$ Therefore the rate of reaction is____$mmol{dm}^{- 3}{s}^{- 1} .$ (Nearest Integer)
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{d\left[c\right]}{dt} = \left(\dfrac{20 - 10}{10}\right) = 1milimole / {dm}^{3}sec$

${\gamma}_{1}A + {\gamma}_{2}B \to {\gamma}_{3}C + {\gamma}_{4}D$

$\dfrac{d\left[D\right]}{dt} = 1 . 5\left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[B\right]\right) = 9milimole / {dm}^{3}sec$

$\left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[B\right]\right) = 2\left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[A\right]\right)$

Rate $= - \dfrac{1}{{\gamma}_{1}}\dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt} = - \dfrac{1}{{\gamma}_{2}}\dfrac{d\left[B\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{{\gamma}_{3}}\dfrac{d\left[C\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{{\gamma}_{4}}\dfrac{d\left[D\right]}{dt}$

(i) $\dfrac{d\left[D\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{{\gamma}_{4}}{{\gamma}_{2}}\left[- \dfrac{d\left[B\right]}{dt}\right] = 1 . 5\left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[B\right]\right)$

$\dfrac{{\gamma}_{4}}{{\gamma}_{2}} = 1 . 5$

(ii) $\dfrac{{\gamma}_{2}}{{\gamma}_{1}}\left[- \dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt}\right] = \left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[B\right]\right) = 2\left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[A\right]\right)$

$\dfrac{{\gamma}_{2}}{{\gamma}_{1}} = 2$

(iii) $\dfrac{d\left[C\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{{\gamma}_{3}}{{\gamma}_{4}}\left[\dfrac{d\left[D\right]}{dt}\right]$

$1 = \dfrac{{\gamma}_{3}}{{\gamma}_{4}} \times 9$

$\dfrac{{\gamma}_{4}}{{\gamma}_{3}} = 9$

So, if

${\gamma}_{3} = 1than{\gamma}_{4} = 9{\gamma}_{2} = 6and{\gamma}_{1} = 3Rateofreaction = \dfrac{1}{{\gamma}_{3}}\dfrac{d [ C ]}{dt} = 1mmol{dm}^{- 3}{s}^{- 1}$
questions.question: For a given chemical reaction ${\gamma}_{1}A + {\gamma}_{2}B \to {\gamma}_{3}C + {\gamma}_{4}D$. Concentration of $C$ changes from $10mmol{dm}^{- 3}$ to $20mmol{dm}^{- 3}$ in $10s .$ Rate of appearance of $D$ is $1 . 5$ times the rate of disappearance of $B$ which is twice the rate of disappearance $A$. The rate of appearance of $D$ has been experimentally determined to be $9mmol{dm}^{- 3}{s}^{- 1} .$ Therefore the rate of reaction is____$mmol{dm}^{- 3}{s}^{- 1} .$ (Nearest Integer)
questions.explanation:
$\dfrac{d\left[c\right]}{dt} = \left(\dfrac{20 - 10}{10}\right) = 1milimole / {dm}^{3}sec$

${\gamma}_{1}A + {\gamma}_{2}B \to {\gamma}_{3}C + {\gamma}_{4}D$

$\dfrac{d\left[D\right]}{dt} = 1 . 5\left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[B\right]\right) = 9milimole / {dm}^{3}sec$

$\left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[B\right]\right) = 2\left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[A\right]\right)$

Rate $= - \dfrac{1}{{\gamma}_{1}}\dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt} = - \dfrac{1}{{\gamma}_{2}}\dfrac{d\left[B\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{{\gamma}_{3}}\dfrac{d\left[C\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{{\gamma}_{4}}\dfrac{d\left[D\right]}{dt}$

(i) $\dfrac{d\left[D\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{{\gamma}_{4}}{{\gamma}_{2}}\left[- \dfrac{d\left[B\right]}{dt}\right] = 1 . 5\left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[B\right]\right)$

$\dfrac{{\gamma}_{4}}{{\gamma}_{2}} = 1 . 5$

(ii) $\dfrac{{\gamma}_{2}}{{\gamma}_{1}}\left[- \dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt}\right] = \left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[B\right]\right) = 2\left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[A\right]\right)$

$\dfrac{{\gamma}_{2}}{{\gamma}_{1}} = 2$

(iii) $\dfrac{d\left[C\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{{\gamma}_{3}}{{\gamma}_{4}}\left[\dfrac{d\left[D\right]}{dt}\right]$

$1 = \dfrac{{\gamma}_{3}}{{\gamma}_{4}} \times 9$

$\dfrac{{\gamma}_{4}}{{\gamma}_{3}} = 9$

So, if

${\gamma}_{3} = 1than{\gamma}_{4} = 9{\gamma}_{2} = 6and{\gamma}_{1} = 3Rateofreaction = \dfrac{1}{{\gamma}_{3}}\dfrac{d [ C ]}{dt} = 1mmol{dm}^{- 3}{s}^{- 1}$

The value of rate constant (k) will increase exponentially with rise in temperature for all type of reactions.

questions.q: The inactivation rate of a viral preparation is proportional to the amount of virus. In the first minute after preparation, $10 %$ of the virus is inactivated. The rate constant for viral inactivation is $___ \times {10}^{- 3}{min}^{- 1} .$ (Nearest integer) [Use : $ln10 = 2 . 303; {\log}_{10}3 = 0 . 477$ property of logarithm$\left: log{x}^{y} = ylogx\right]$
questions.solution:
As the unit of rate constant is ${min}^{- 1}$ so it must be a first order reaction
$k \times t = 2 . 303{logA}_{0} / {A}_{t}$
in $1$ min $10 %$ is inactivated so taking
${A}_{0} = 100{A}_{t} = 90$ in $1min$
So $k \times 1 = 2 . 303 \times log\dfrac{100}{90}$

$= 2 . 303 \times ( log10 - 2log3 )$
$= 2 . 303 \times ( 1 - 2 \times 0 . 477 )$
$= 0 . 10593$

$= 105 . 93 \times {10}^{- 3}$
Answer is $106$

questions.q:
The reaction $2A + {B}_{2} \to 2AB$ is an elementary reaction.

For a certain quantity of reactants, if the volume of the reaction vessel is reduced by a factor of $3,$ the rate of the reaction increases by a factor of _____ . (Round off to the Nearest Integer).
questions.solution:
Reaction : $2A + {B}_{2} ⟶ 2AB$

As the reaction is elementary, the rate of reaction is

$r = K . [ A{]}^{2}\left[{B}_{2}\right]$

on reducing the volume by a factor of $3,$ the concentrations of $A$ and ${B}_{2}$ will become 3 times and hence, the rate becomes ${3}^{2} \times 3 = 27$ times of initial rate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $A$ and $B$ decompose via first order kinetics with half-lives $54 . 0min$ and $18 . 0min$ respectively. Starting from an equimolar non-reactive mixture of $A$ and $B$, the time taken for the concentration of $A$ to become $16$ times that of $B$ is ______ $min$. (Round off to the Nearest Integer).
questions.solution:
Given $A = {t}_{1 / 2} = 54min$

$B = {t}_{1 / 2} = 18min$

$t = 0$ '$x$' $M t = 0$ '$x$' $M$

$⇒$ To calculate : $\left[{A}_{t}\right] = 16 \times \left[{B}_{t}\right] time $= ?

$⇒$ For $I$ order kinetic : $\left[{A}_{t}\right] = \dfrac{{A}_{0}}{{\left(2\right)}^{n}}$

$n \to$ no. of Half lives

$⇒$ Now from the relation $( 1 )$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{{\left(2\right)}^{{n}_{1}}} = \dfrac{x}{{\left(2\right)}^{{n}_{2}}} \times 16 ⇒ {\left(2\right)}^{{n}_{2}} = {\left(2\right)}^{{n}_{1}} \times {\left(2\right)}^{4}$

$⇒ {n}_{2} = {n}_{1} + 4 ⇒ \dfrac{t}{{\left({t}_{1 / 2}\right)}_{2}} = \dfrac{t}{{\left({t}_{1 / 2}\right)}_{1}} + 4$

$⇒ t\left(\dfrac{1}{18} - \dfrac{1}{54}\right) = 4 ⇒ t = \dfrac{4 \times 18 \times 54}{36}$

$⇒ t = 108min$

questions.solution:
Fraction of molecules to have enough energy to react $= {e}^{- Ea / RT}$

So, $x = \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{RT}$

$= \dfrac{80 . 9 \times {10}^{3}}{8 . 31 \times 700}$

$= 13 . 9 \approx 14$

questions.q: The rate constant of a reaction increases by five times on increase in temperature from $27 ° C to 52 ° C$. The value of activation energy in ${kJmol}^{- 1}$ is ___ .(Rounded-off to the nearest integer) $\left[R = 8 . 314J{K}^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}\right]$
questions.solution:
${T}_{1} = 300K, {T}_{2} = 325K, {K}_{2} = 5K$

$ln\dfrac{{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1}} = \dfrac{Ea}{R}\left[\dfrac{1}{{T}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{T}_{2}}\right]$

or, $ln5 = \dfrac{Ea}{8 . 314}\left[\dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1}{325}\right]$

or, $Ea = 0 . 7 \times 2 . 303 \times 8 . 314 \times 12 \times 325$

$= 52271J = 52 . 271kJ$

Nearest integer answer will be $52kJ$

The temperature at which the rate constant of the reaction is ${10}^{- 4}{s}^{- 1}$ is _____ $K .$

$\left|Slope\right| = \dfrac{Ea}{2 . 303R} = 10, 000$

${T}_{2} = 526 . 31 ≃ 526K$

Hence answer is $\left(526\right)$

questions.q:
Sucrose hydrolyses in acid solution into glucose and fructose following first order rate law with a half-life of $3 . 33h$ at $25 ° C .$ After $9h,$ the fraction of sucrose remaining is $f .$ The value of ${\log}_{10}\left(\dfrac{1}{f}\right)$ is ________ $\times {10}^{- 2} .$ (Rounded off to the nearest integer)

[Assume: In$10 = 2 . 303, ln2 = 0 . 693$]
questions.solution:
${C}_{12}{H}_{22}{O}_{11} + {H}_{2}O\mathop{\to}_{{t}_{1 / 2} = \dfrac{10}{3}hr}^{order}\mathop{{C}_{6}{H}_{12}{O}_{6}}_{Glucose} + \mathop{{C}_{6}{H}_{12}{O}_{6}}_{Fructose}$

$t = 0a = {\left[A\right]}_{0}$

$t = 9hra - x = {\left[A\right]}_{t}$

from I order kinetic: $\dfrac{k \times t}{2 . 303} = log\dfrac{{\left|A\right|}_{0}}{{\left|A\right|}_{t}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{ln2 \times 9}{\dfrac{10}{3} \times 2 . 303} = log\left(\dfrac{1}{f}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{0 . 693 \times 9 \times 3}{23 . 03} = log\left(\dfrac{1}{f}\right)$

$⇒ log\left(\dfrac{1}{f}\right) = 0 . 81246 = 81 . 24 \times {10}^{- 2}$

$⇒ x = 81$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A flask contains a mixture of compounds $A$ and $B$. Both compounds decompose by first-order kinetics. The half-lives for $A$ and $B$ are $300s$ and $180s$, respectively. If the concentrations of $A$ and $B$ are equal initially, the time required for the concentration of A to be four times that of $B$ (in s) is : $( Useln2 = 0 . 693 )$
questions.solution:
${C}_{t} = {C}_{0}{e}^{- kt}$

${k}_{A} = \dfrac{ln2}{300}$\left(k = \dfrac{ln2}{{T}_{1 / 2}}\right)$

${k}_{B} = \dfrac{ln2}{180}$

${\left({C}_{t}\right)}_{A} = {\left({C}_{0}\right)}_{A}{e}^{- {k}_{A}t}$

${\left({C}_{t}\right)}_{B} = {\left({C}_{0}\right)}_{B}{e}^{- {k}_{B}t}$

$\dfrac{{\left({C}_{t}\right)}_{, B}}{\left({C}_{t}\right), A} = \dfrac{{\left({C}_{0}\right)}_{, B}}{\left({C}_{0}\right), A} \times {e}^{\left({k}_{A} - {k}_{B}\right)t}$

$\dfrac{1}{4} = {e}^{\left({k}_{A} - {k}_{B}\right)t}$

$ln\dfrac{1}{4} = \left[\dfrac{ln2}{300} - \dfrac{ln2}{180}\right]t$

$- 2ln2 = \left[\dfrac{ln2}{300} - \dfrac{ln2}{180}\right]t$

$2 = \left(\dfrac{120}{180 \times 300}\right)t$

$t = \dfrac{2 \times 180 \times 300}{120} = 900sec$

questions.q: It is true that:
options: A second order reaction is always a multistep reaction
A zero order reaction is a multi-step reaction
A first order reaction is always a single step reaction
A zero order reaction is a single step reaction
questions.solution: For elementary reaction, order is equal to stoichiometric coefficient. Since reaction having zero stoichiometric coefficient is meaningless therefore, zero order reaction is complex reaction or multi-step reaction.

$ln\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) \times 8 .3 \times 1200 = {E}_{a}$
$⟹ {E}_{a} = 0 .4 \times 8 .3 \times 1200$
$⟹ {E}_{a} = 3984\dfrac{J}{mol} .$
$⟹ {E}_{a} = 3 .984 k\dfrac{J}{mol} .$

questions.q: The rate of a certain biochemical reaction at physiological temperature $\left(T\right)$ occurs ${10}^{6}$ times faster with enzyme than without. The change in the activation energy upon adding enzyme is:
questions.solution:
$K = {Ae}^{- E / RT} . . . . . . ( 1 )$

${10}^{6}\text{K} = {Ae}^{- {E}_{c}RT} \ldots \ldots . ( 2 )$

On dividing eq, 2 by eq, 1

${10}^{6} = {e}^{\left(E - {E}_{c}\right) / RT}$

on taking logarithm both sides

$6ln10 = \dfrac{\left(E - {E}_{c}\right)}{RT}$

$2 .303 \times 6 = \dfrac{\left(E - {E}_{c}\right)}{RT}$
$E - {E}_{c} = 2 .303 \times ( 6RT )$

${\Delta E}_{a} = {E}_{c} - E = - 2 .303 \times 6RT$

questions.q: During the nuclear explosion, one of the products is ${}^{90}Sr$ with half life of $6.93$ years. If $1\mug$ of ${}^{90}Sr$ was absorbed in the bones of a newly born baby in place of $Ca,$ how much time, in years, is required to reduce it by $90%$ if it is not lost metabolically ____________.
questions.solution:
Radioactive disintegration is always a first order reaction for a first order reaction. Radioactive decay is the process by which an unstable atomic nucleus loses energy by radiation.

$Kt = 2.303log\dfrac{\left[{A}_{o}\right]}{\left[{A}_{t}\right]}$

where $\left[{A}_{o}\right] =$ initial concentration

$\left[{A}_{t}\right] =$ concentration at time ‘t’

${t}_{\dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{0.693}{K} K = \dfrac{0.693}{{t}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}} = \dfrac{0.693}{6.93} ⇒ 0.1yent{s}^{- 1} {t}_{90%} = \dfrac{2.303}{0.1} log\dfrac{\left[100\right]}{\left[10\right]} {t}_{90%} = 23.03$ years.

$\left(R = 8.314J{K}^{- 1}mo{l}^{- 1}\right)$
questions.solution:
${T}_{2} = {527}^{o}C ⇒ 800k; {k}_{1} = 2.5 \times {10}^{- 4}$

${T}_{1} = {327}^{o}C ⇒ 600k; {k}_{2} = 1$

$ln ⁡ \dfrac{{k}_{2}}{{k}_{1}} = - \dfrac{Ea}{R}\left(\dfrac{1}{{T}_{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{T}_{1}}\right)$

$ln ⁡ \left(4000\right) = \dfrac{Ea}{8.314}\left(\dfrac{1}{2400}\right)$

$Ea = 165.431kJ, Ea \approx 166kJ / mol$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A bacterial infection in an internal wound grows as ${N}^{'}\left(t\right) = {N}_{0}exp ⁡ ( t )$ , where the time $t$ is in hours. A dose of antibiotic, taken orally, needs 1 hour to reach the wound. Once it reaches there, the bacterial population goes down as $\dfrac{dN}{dt} = - 5{N}^{2}$ . What will be the plot of $\dfrac{{N}_{0}}{N}$ vs $t$ after $1$ hour?
questions.solution:
From 0 to 1 hour, ${N}^{'} = {N}_{0}{e}^{t}$
From 1 hour onwards $\dfrac{dN}{dt} = - 5{N}^{2}$
So at $t = 1$ hour, ${N}^{'} = e{N}_{0}$
$\dfrac{dN}{dt} = - 5{N}^{2}$
${∫}_{e{N}_{0}}^{N}{N}^{- 2}dN = - 5{∫}_{1}^{t}dt$
$\dfrac{1}{N} - \dfrac{1}{e{N}_{0}} = 5\left(t - 1\right)$
$\dfrac{{N}_{0}}{N} - \dfrac{1}{e} = 5{N}_{0} ( t - 1 )$
$\dfrac{{N}_{0}}{N} = 5{N}_{0} ( t - 1 ) + \dfrac{1}{e}$
$\dfrac{{N}_{0}}{N} = 5{N}_{0}t + \left(\dfrac{1}{e} - 5{N}_{0}\right)$
Which is following $y = mx + C$

questions.q: For an elementary chemical reaction, ${A}_{2}\mathop{⇄}_{{k}_{- 1}}^{{k}_{1}}2A$ , the expression for $\dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt}$ is:
questions.solution:
For the reaction, ${A}_{2}\overset{{K}_{1}}{\to}2A$

${r}_{f} = - \dfrac{d\left[{A}_{2}\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(\dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt}\right)}_{1} = {K}_{1}\left[{A}_{2}\right]$

${\left(\dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt}\right)}_{1} = 2{K}_{1}\left[{A}_{2}\right]$

For the reaction, $2A\overset{{k}_{- 1}}{\to}{A}_{2}$

${r}_{b} = - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(\dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt}\right)}_{2} = {K}_{- 1}{\left[A\right]}^{2}$

${\left(\dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt}\right)}_{2} = - 2{K}_{- 1}{\left[A\right]}^{2}$

Hence, the overall rate is given by:

$\dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt} = 2{k}_{1}\left[{A}_{2}\right] - 2{k}_{- 1}{\left[A\right]}^{2}$

For the reaction, $2A + B \to$ products, when the concentration of $A$ and $B$ both were doubled, the rate of the reaction increased from $0.3mol{L}^{- 1}{s}^{- 1}$ to $2.4mol{L}^{- 1}{s}^{- 1} .$ When the concentration of $A$ alone is doubled, the rate increased from $0.3mol{L}^{- 1}{s}^{- 1}$ to $0.6mol{L}^{- 1}{s}^{- 1} .$

Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Order of the reaction with respect to $B$  is  $2$
Total order of the reaction is $4$
Order of the reaction with respect to $A$  is $2$
Order of the reaction with respect to $B$ is $1$
questions.solution:
$2A + B \to C$

Initial ${r}_{1} = k{\left[A\right]}^{x}{\left[B\right]}^{y} = 0.3m / sec$ ...(i)

${r}_{2} = k{\left[2A\right]}^{x}{\left[2B\right]}^{y} = 2.4$ ...(ii)

${r}_{3} = k{\left[2A\right]}^{x}{\left[B\right]}^{y} = 0.6$ ...(iii)

From (i) $\div$ (iii)

${\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{x}{\left(1\right)}^{y} = \dfrac{0.3}{0.6}$

${\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{x} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$x = 1$

(ii) $\div$ (iii)

$\dfrac{{r}_{2}}{{r}_{3}} = \dfrac{2.4}{0.6} = {\left(2\right)}^{y}$

$4 = {\left(2\right)}^{y}$

$y = 2$

The order of reaction w.r.t. $A = 1$ and w.r.t. $B = 2$

Total order of reaction $= 1 + 2 = 3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If 50 % of a reaction occurs in 100 second and 75 % of the reaction occurs in 200 second, the order of this reaction is:
questions.solution:
50% of a reaction occurs in 100 second and 75% of the reaction occurs in 200 second, the order of this reaction is 1.

Let the initial reactant concentration is 1 M.

In the first 100 seconds, reactant concentration is reduced to $50 % or1 \times \dfrac{50}{100} ​ = 0 . 5M .$

In the second 100 seconds (total 200 seconds from start), reactant concentration is reduced to $100 - 75 = 25 % or1 \times \dfrac{25}{100} ​ = 0 . 25M .$.

Thus, we observe that after each 100 second period, the reactant concentration is reduced to one half. Hence, 100 seconds is the half-life period and is independent of reactant concentration. This is characteristic of the first-order reaction.



First-order reaction as the half-life is constant.

questions.q:
The rate of a reaction quadruples when the temperature changes from $300$ to $310K$ . The activation energy of this reaction is:

(Assume Activation energy and pre-exponential factor are independent of temperature; $ln ( 2 ) = 0 . 693; R = 8 . 314J{mol}^{- 1}{K}^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
The activation energy, rate constant and temperature can be related using Arrhenius equation.

$k = {Ae}^{- \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{RT}}$

$ln\left(\dfrac{{k}_{2}}{{k}_{1}}\right) = \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{R}\left(\dfrac{1}{{T}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{T}_{2}}\right)$

$ln\left(4\right) = \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{R}\left(\dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1}{310}\right)$

$2 \times 0 . 693 = \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{R}\left(\dfrac{10}{300 \times 310}\right)$

${\text{E}}_{\text{a}} = \dfrac{2 \times 0.693 \times 300 \times 310 \times 8.314}{10} = 107.2\text{kJ/mol}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The rate of a reaction A doubles on increasing the temperature from$300to310K$. By how much, the temperature of reaction B should be increased from $300K$ so that rate doubles if activation energy of the reaction B is twice to that of reaction A.
questions.solution:
$log2 = \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{R}\left\{\dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1}{310}\right\}$ .......(i)

$log 2 =2 \left[\dfrac{{E}_{a}}{R}\left\{\dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1}{T}\right\}\right]$ ......(ii)

$\dfrac{2{E}_{a}}{R}\left\{\dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1}{T}\right\} = \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{R}\left\{\dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1}{310}\right\}$

$\dfrac{1}{300} + \dfrac{1}{310} = \dfrac{2}{T}$

$⇒ T = \dfrac{300 \times 310}{610} \times 2$

$= 304.92$

Hence, the temperature of reaction B should be increased from $300K$ by $304 . 92 - 300 = 4 . 92K$.

questions.q:
The reaction of ozone with oxygen atoms in the presence of chlorine atoms can occur by a two step process shown below:

${O}_{3}\left(g\right) + {Cl}^{•} \to {O}_{2}\left(g\right) + {ClO}^{•}\left(g\right)$ ...(i)

${ClO}^{•}\left(g\right) + {O}^{•}\left(g\right) \to {O}_{2}\left(g\right) + {Cl}^{•}\left(g\right)$ ...(ii)

${k}_{ii} = 2.6 \times {10}^{10}Lmo{l}^{- 1}{s}^{- 1}$

The closest rate constant for the overall reaction

_________________________________

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$A + 2B \to C$ , the rate equation for the reaction is given as

Rate $= k[ A ][ B ]$

If the concentration of A is kept the same but that of B is doubled what will happen to the rate itself?
questions.solution:
The order of the overall reaction is 2.

Rate $= k [ A ] [ B ] = R$

${R}^{'} = k [ A ] [ 2B ]$

$\dfrac{R}{{R}^{'}} = \dfrac{k [ A ] [ B ]}{k [ A ] [ 2B ]} = \dfrac{k [ A ] [ B ]}{2k [ A ] [ B ]}$

$⇒ 2R = {R}^{'}$ i.e, rate become doubles.

questions.q: For the equilibrium, $A\left(g\right) ⇌ B\left(g\right), ∆ His - 40kJ / mol$ . If the ratio of the activation energies of the forward $\left({E}_{f}\right)$ and reverse $\left({E}_{b}\right)$ reactions is $\dfrac{2}{3}$ then:
questions.solution:
Activation energy is the minimum amount of energy that must be provided for compounds to result in a chemical reaction.

$A\left(g\right) ⇌ B\left(g\right); ∆ H = - 40$ kJ/mole

$∆ H = {E}_{a\left(f\right)} - {E}_{a\left(b\right)} = - 40kJ$

$\dfrac{{E}_{a\left(f\right)}}{{E}_{a\left(b\right)}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ {E}_{a\left(f\right)} = \dfrac{2}{3}{E}_{a\left(b\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{3}{E}_{a\left(b\right)} - {E}_{a\left(b\right)} = - \dfrac{{E}_{a\left(b\right)}}{3} = - 40kJ$

${E}_{a\left(b\right)} = + 120kJ$

${E}_{a\left(f\right)} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 120 = 80kJ$

questions.q: The reaction $2{N}_{2}{O}_{5}\left(g\right) \to 4N{O}_{2}\left(g\right) + {O}_{2} ( g )$ follows first order kinetics. The pressure of a vessel containing only ${N}_{2}{O}_{5}$ was found to increase from 50 mm Hg to 87.5 mm Hg in 30 min. The pressure exerted by the gases after 60 min. Will be (Assume temperature remains constant) :
questions.solution:
$2{N}_{2}{O}_{5}\left(g\right) \to 4N{O}_{2}\left(g\right) + {O}_{2}\left(g\right)$

at t=0, P0 0 0

at t=30 min. (P0-x) 2x $\dfrac{x}{2}$

at t=60 min. (P0-y) 2y $\dfrac{y}{2}$

$∵ {P}_{0} = 50mmHg$

$∵ after30min .$⟹ \left({P}_{0} - x\right) + 2x + \dfrac{x}{2} = 87.5$

${P}_{0} + \dfrac{3}{2}x = 87.5$

$\dfrac{3}{2}x = 37.5; x = 25mmHg$

${P}_{0} = 50; {P}_{30min} = 25mmHg$

That mean 30 min. is Half life of reaction.

${P}_{0}\overset{30min .}{\to}\dfrac{{P}_{0}}{2}\overset{30min .}{\to}\dfrac{{P}_{0}}{4}$

at t= 60 min

${P}_{{N}_{2}{O}_{5}} = \dfrac{{P}_{0}}{4} ⟹ \dfrac{50}{4} = 12.5mmHg$

${P}_{0} - y = 12.5 ⟹ 50 - y = 12.5$

$y = 37.5mmHg$

Total P after 60 min. $⟹ \left({P}_{0} - y\right) + 2y + \dfrac{y}{2} ⟹ 50 \times \dfrac{3}{2} \times 37.5$

$= 106.25mmHg$

When concentration of $\mathrm{B}$ alone was doubled, the half-life did not change. When the concentration of $\mathrm{A}$ alone was doubled, the rate increased by two times. The unit of rate constant for this reaction is
questions.solution:

When conc. of $\mathrm{B}$ is doubled, the half life did not change, hence reaction is of first order w.r.t. $\mathrm{B}$. 
When concentration of $\mathrm{A}$ is doubled, reaction rate is doubled, hence reaction is of first order w.r.t. $\mathrm{A}$. 
Hence over all order of reaction is $1+1=2$
So, unit of rate constant $\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \mathrm{~lit~s}^{-1}$.
Hence, (A) is correct.

questions.q: A radioactive element gets spilled over the floor of a room. Its half-life period is $30$ days. If the initial activity is ten times the permissible value, after how many days will it be safe to enter the room?
questions.solution:
Activity $\left(-\frac{\mathrm{dN}}{\mathrm{dt}}\right) \propto \mathrm{N}\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{N}_{\circ}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\mathrm{n}} \frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{N}_{\circ}}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\mathrm{n}}\frac{1}{10}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\mathrm{n}} \Rightarrow 10=2^{\mathrm{n}} \log 10=\mathrm{nlog} 2\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=\frac{1}{0.301}=3.32\mathrm{t}=\mathrm{n} \times \mathrm{t}_{112}=3.32 \times 30=99.6 \text{ days }$
Hence, (D) is correct.
